title: Nexus Mods Mandates AI Disclosures for All New Uploads
summary: PC gaming's largest mod repository now requires creators to declare AI use in uploads. Nexus Mods announces mandatory AI disclosure policy effective today.
body_markdown:
#### 💡 TL;DR


- Nexus Mods now requires all creators to disclose whether AI was used in their mod uploads starting today.
- The policy aims to provide transparency without banning AI-generated content from the platform entirely.
- Mod authors must declare AI involvement during upload, giving users informed choice about what they download.


Nexus Mods, the largest repository for[PC gaming](https://emergent.sh/ai-web-app-builder/gaming) modifications, has introduced a mandatory AI disclosure requirement for all new uploads. Starting November 3, 2026, mod creators must declare whether artificial intelligence played any role in their work, marking a significant shift in how the gaming community approaches AI-generated content. The policy stops short of banning AI entirely but prioritizes transparency for the platform's millions of users.


## What the New Policy Requires


Under the updated guidelines, every mod author uploading new content must explicitly state whether AI tools were used during creation. The disclosure appears during the upload process and becomes visible to users browsing the repository. Nexus Mods clarified that this applies to all forms of AI assistance, from generating textures and character models to writing dialogue or scripting gameplay mechanics.


The platform emphasized that the requirement covers both fully AI-generated content and hybrid approaches where creators use AI as one tool among many. Mod authors who fail to provide accurate disclosures risk having their content removed or facing account restrictions. This enforcement mechanism ensures the policy carries real weight rather than serving as an optional courtesy.


## Release Date and Immediate Impact


The policy was officially launched on November 3, 2026, following months of community discussion about AI's role in modding. Nexus Mods announced the change in a detailed post addressing ongoing debates within the PC gaming community about creative authenticity and automation. The timing reflects growing industry-wide conversations about AI transparency across digital content platforms.


Existing mods uploaded before the policy's implementation are not retroactively affected, though the platform encourages authors to voluntarily add AI disclosures to older work. This grandfathering approach minimizes disruption to the repository's existing catalog of hundreds of thousands of mods while ensuring future uploads meet the new standard.


## Why Transparency Over Bans


Nexus Mods chose mandatory disclosure rather than an outright AI ban, recognizing the technology's growing presence in creative workflows. The platform stated that users deserve to know how content was created without dictating which tools are acceptable. This stance acknowledges that some players prefer entirely human-created mods while others remain neutral or supportive of AI assistance.


The approach mirrors emerging content labeling standards in other creative industries, from stock photography to music production. By making AI involvement visible, Nexus Mods empowers users to filter content according to their preferences while allowing creators who use AI tools to continue sharing their work. The policy also creates a clearer ethical framework for the modding community as AI capabilities advance.


## Community Reaction and Broader Context


Response from the modding community has been mixed. Some creators welcome the transparency requirement, arguing it protects artists who build mods without AI from being unfairly compared to rapidly-produced automated content. Others view the disclosure mandate as unnecessary bureaucracy or worry it will stigmatize legitimate AI-assisted workflows that still involve significant human creativity.


The policy arrives as major game developers and platforms grapple with similar questions about AI-generated content. Steam, Epic Games Store, and other distributors have faced pressure to establish clear guidelines as generative AI becomes more sophisticated. Nexus Mods' approach may influence how other user-generated content platforms balance innovation with community values.


## What This Means


Nexus Mods has set a precedent for transparency in gaming's creator economy without restricting the tools artists can use. The mandatory disclosure system gives players informed choice while acknowledging that AI is becoming a standard part of many creative workflows. As the technology evolves, this middle-ground approach could become a model for other platforms wrestling with similar challenges. The policy's success will depend on consistent enforcement and community buy-in, but it represents a pragmatic step toward addressing AI's role in user-generated content.
